Below that is one uniform white face down to row 17, with no front-edge line or eave shadow. A blue band (rows 18-19), a dark window (rows 20-25) and a slot panel (rows 26-31) follow. styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is two small props (a red postbox and a vending machine), not a roofed building, so the kind match is only loose. Judged on craft, the measured facts favour it: 18 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels. That means the outlines lean toward the material colour (dark red beside the postbox, dark blue-grey beside the machine casing) rather than being a black sticker line. The postbox cylinder shows highlight, mid and shadow bands plus a label. The vending machine has a frame, a lit panel and a grid of coloured buttons that break up the surface. Each material ramp has about 4 steps, slightly fewer than Beodeul's 5-6, and the pale machine face is the flattest area. Even so, there are no large flat 5x5 fills and the tile density matches the references, so a careful artist would likely accept it next to them.
